keyAction.next: next field (in the last one — save the row)
keyAction.more: another value in the same place
keyAction.save: save the row and start the next

node.pickSays: An existing entry (language, topic) chosen once at the top — it stays for all rows until you change it.
node.entrySays: An entry made from every row (or reused if one like it already exists).

plan.cycle: The form has a loop — fix it in Schemes (Ways of adding).
plan.tooMany: {label}: one row would make {n} entries — check “several in a row”.

problem.noEntry: Add at least one entry “in every row”.
problem.takesNothing: “{node}” takes nothing from the row — the same entry would be made for every row.
problem.goneField: “{node}”: a connection leads to a field that no longer exists.
problem.manyToOne: “{node}” can have several entries, but the field “{field}” takes one — a separate entry will be made for each.
problem.cantType: “{node}”: the field “{field}” cannot be typed in the form.
problem.cantSet: “{node}”: the field “{field}” cannot be set in the form.
problem.nothingTyped: No field is typed in the row — there would be nothing to add.

describe.picks: At the start you choose: {list}. The choice stays for all rows until you change it.
describe.withPlace: , with the place typed in the row
describe.choices: For each value a kind is chosen: {list}; in a list — a prefix, e.g. “{example}: …”.
describe.pairs: One for each pair ({fields} takes one entry).
describe.needs: Made only when the row has {list}.
describe.reuse: If one like it already exists (the same: {fields}), it is used and missing values are added.
describe.alwaysNew: A new one is always made.
describe.values: ; separate several values in a cell with {sep}
describe.paste: Pasting a list: one line is one row{sep}{many}.

edit.noRoot: This form has no entry that joins the fields of a row — editing shows only the first column.
edit.notEmpty: “{row}”: {field} cannot be empty — delete the whole row.

rows.none: With this choice at the start there are no rows yet.

run.readOnly: In this knowledge base you can only read.
run.askDiscard: Discard unsaved changes? The changes in the rows will be lost.
run.noFields: This form has no fields typed in a row —
run.askUndo: Delete {n} added entries? They stay in the version history.

paste.title: Paste a list
paste.hint: One line — one row; columns in order: {columns}. You can paste straight from a spreadsheet.
paste.values: Several values in a cell are separated by
paste.wide: · {n} lines have more columns — the rest went into the last one
paste.example:
e.g.
car, automobile	Auto
dog	Hund

editor.createFailed: The form could not be created.
editor.intro: An add form says what is made from one row — e.g. two words and the translation between them — and what you choose once at the start (languages, topic). Start from the kind you want to add.
editor.foreign: From “{name}” — read-only here (you can fill it in).
editor.name: Form name
editor.askDelete: Delete the form “{name}”? Entries added with it stay.
editor.order: Order of fields in a row
editor.says: A word for those filling it in (optional)
editor.unsavedNote: You have unsaved changes: the export contains them, and an import of the same form (“ref”) will replace them with the saved one.
editor.orderNone: Nothing is typed in a row yet.
editor.orderHint: In this order you type the fields (Enter) and the columns of a pasted list stand — and in this order they go into a field that takes several entries (e.g. psalm, psalm, hymn).
editor.addEntry: Add an entry made from every row
editor.wireHint: Connect an entry's dot (on the right) to a field's dot (on the left) — or choose “from where” at the field in the node settings.
editor.otherKindHint: In the row, a kind is chosen for each value.
editor.label: Name in the form
editor.many: Several in one row (e.g. two words with the same meaning)
editor.optional: Can stay empty — the entries it leads to are made without it too
editor.reuse: When such an entry already exists
editor.reuseSame: use it (and add what it lacks)
editor.locatorTyped: place (e.g. the verse “Lk 1:35”) typed in every row
editor.newPick: a new choice at the start
